mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.3 percentage points or more signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 3% or more signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.75 percentage points signals a tightening monetary cycle, which raises discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous earnings surprise.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of 1.5% or more combined with a 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of 10% or more signals a synchronized collapse in consumption and housing demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 1.5% AND HOUST falls > 10% over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of 50,000 or more combined with a monthly unemployment rate increase of 0.2 percentage points or more signals accelerating labor market weakness, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > 50,000 AND UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 2% or more combined with a 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of 1% or more signals a synchronized supply-demand contraction, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% AND GDPC1 falls > 1% over 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous monetary easing.
